title: City Council District 9
statement: What I'm taking up this week is Laurel, and I'm not going to dress it up. The sentiment reading is -0.03 against a city at 0.115, and the crime index is 0.69 against 0.655 — Laurel is the outlier on my turf, and a steady trajectory is not the same as a good one. Retail vitality dropped sharply while Uptown climbed, and the missed pickup that cost Laurel sentiment is the kind of small, unglamorous failure that tells you the basics are slipping. I'm not going to pretend the answer is a new program. I'm proposing the city put real attention on the patching that Laurel needs — the visible, on-the-ground work that says somebody is paying attention. My district, my name, and I'll report back on what actually moves.

payload.title: Laurel Neighborhood Patch and Clean-Up
payload.problem: Targeted street-level repair and cleanup work in Laurel — fixing the visible conditions that erode confidence and sending the message that this district is not being left behind. Covers patching, missed-pickup recovery, and the small physical stuff that residents read as care.
